summary: A narrowly scoped developmental-kernel calibration: a scripted common action/outcome life feeds recurrent evidence-constrained dream proposals, deterministic support and compilation, a per-life LoRA transport, and a frozen goal-conditioned reader/thinker. It tests whether recurrent compiled LoRA improves held-out compositional action beyond matched direct-QA LoRA while explicitly excluding on-policy flywheel and broad intelligence claims.
system_thesis: An organism can convert consequences of lived actions into an increasingly connected experiential world approximation; recurrent dream-time local connection growth and re-expression may be consolidated into per-life parametric associations, while a goal-conditioned thinker retrieves, composes, plans, and revises those associations for later action. The LoRA is only a lossy transport organ: discovery and behavior, where present, belong to the complete evidence-constrained organism. This fixed-deck pilot isolates a bounded middle segment of that thesis and deliberately does not test the later feedback loop in which policy-selected thinking and outcomes change future dream cycles.
title: Developmental kernel pilot v1: recurrent sleep-compiled per-life LoRA calibration
